title: Securing User-Generated Content in Collaborative Dashboards
business: A collaborative project management platform where users share dynamic status updates and custom dashboard widgets.
problem: Malicious actors inject unauthorized JavaScript into shared dashboard widgets, which executes in the browser of other users, leading to session hijacking or unauthorized data exfiltration.
solution: Implement a Defense in Depth strategy by enforcing strict output encoding and utilizing a Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict script execution to trusted origins only.
steps: Identify all points where user-provided data is rendered in the dashboard UI.
Apply context-aware output encoding to convert special characters into their safe HTML entity equivalents before rendering.
Configure a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) header to disable inline script execution and restrict script sources to known, trusted domains.
Validate all incoming widget configurations against a strict schema to prevent structural injection.
outcome: The platform prevents arbitrary script execution, ensuring that even if malicious data is stored, it remains inert and harmless when viewed by other users.
limitation: Strict output encoding can sometimes break legitimate rich-text formatting if not implemented with context-awareness; verify by testing complex inputs against the rendering engine.
